title: -(으)ㄹ게요와 -(으)ㄹ 거예요: 약속할 때와 계획을 말할 때
summary: -(으)ㄹ게요 and -(으)ㄹ 거예요 both mean "I will", but -(으)ㄹ게요 is only for a promise or decision made in response to the listener. Use -(으)ㄹ 거예요 for reported plans, other people's plans, and questions.
objective: Learners can form -(으)ㄹ게요 correctly (spelled 게, not 께) and choose between it and -(으)ㄹ 거예요.
exercises: Change the verb in brackets to the -(으)ㄹ게요 form. (a) 천천히 오세요. 제가 여기서 ( 기다리다 ). (b) 택배는 제가 ( 받다 ). (c) 요리하는 동안 제가 아이들하고 ( 놀다 ).
Change both verbs to the -(으)ㄹ게요 form. 싣다 = to load, 줍다 = to pick up. A: 캠핑 끝났네요. 짐도 많고 바닥에 쓰레기도 있어요. B: 짐은 제가 차에 ( 싣다 ). 쓰레기도 제가 ( 줍다 ).
One word in B's answer is spelled wrong. Find it and correct it. A: 밖에 바람이 많이 불어요. B: 그럼 두꺼운 코트를 입을께요.
Choose the natural answer in each dialogue. (a) A: 동생은 방학에 뭐 해요? B: 동생은 수영을 ( 배울게요 / 배울 거예요 ). (b) A: 내일 몇 시에 ( 출발할게요 / 출발할 거예요 )? B: 아침 8시요.
Choose the natural answer for each blank. A: 이번 주말에 뭐 해요? B: 친구하고 영화를 ( 볼게요 / 볼 거예요 ). A: 아, 저도 그 영화 보고 싶었어요! B: 그래요? 그럼 같이 봐요. 표는 제가 ( 예매할게요 / 예매할 거예요 ).
answers: (a) 기다릴게요 (b) 받을게요 (✗ 발을게요. 받다 is a regular verb.) (c) 놀게요 (✗ 놀을게요)
입을께요 → 입을게요 (It is pronounced [이블께요], but it is always written 게.)
(a) 배울 거예요 (The subject is a third person, 동생.) (b) 출발할 거예요 (It is a question.)
볼 거예요 / 예매할게요 (The first is a plan B is just reporting. The second is a promise B makes after hearing what A said.)

forms.when: The verb stem ends in a vowel.
forms.means: A promise or decision the speaker makes to the listener, e.g. 연락하다 → 연락할게요, 가다 → 갈게요
forms.exampleMeaning: I'll get back to you tomorrow.

forms.when: The verb stem ends in a consonant (받침) other than ㄹ.
forms.means: The same meaning. Add 을 and do not change the stem, e.g. 먹다 → 먹을게요, 닫다 → 닫을게요, 잡다 → 잡을게요
forms.example: A: 음식이 좀 남았네요. B: 남은 건 제가 먹을게요.
forms.exampleMeaning: A: There's a bit of food left over. B: I'll eat what's left.

forms.when: The verb stem ends in ㄹ.
forms.means: Keep the ㄹ and add only 게요. Do not add 을, e.g. 만들다 → 만들게요 (✗ 만들을게요), 열다 → 열게요

forms.when: The verb is a ㄷ-irregular verb, such as 걷다 or 묻다 (to ask).
forms.means: The ㄷ changes to ㄹ before 을, e.g. 걷다 → 걸을게요, 묻다 → 물을게요
forms.example: A: 택시 부를까요? B: 아니요, 가까우니까 걸을게요.
forms.exampleMeaning: A: Shall I call a taxi? B: No, it's close, so I'll walk.

forms.when: The verb is a ㅂ-irregular verb, such as 돕다 or 굽다.
forms.means: The ㅂ drops, 우 is added, then ㄹ게요, e.g. 돕다 → 도울게요
forms.exampleMeaning: I'll help you when you move.

forms.when: Use this for other people's plans, for questions, and for your own plans that have nothing to do with the listener.
forms.means: A plan or intention you are simply reporting. It is not a promise to the listener.
forms.example: A: 주말에 뭐 해요? B: 집에서 쉴 거예요.
forms.exampleMeaning: A: What are you doing this weekend? B: I'm going to rest at home.

watchOut: Don't use -(으)ㄹ게요 when the subject is someone else. It is only for your own promise. ✗ 지수 씨가 이따가 전화할게요. → ✓ 지수 씨가 이따가 전화할 거예요.
Don't use -(으)ㄹ게요 in questions. ✗ 일을 언제 끝낼게요? → ✓ 언제 끝낼 거예요?
It is pronounced [께요] but written 게요. ✗ 할께요 → ✓ 할게요
